title: pravapis W-name inventory row
description: Names whose initial Ў renders English W rather than Збор правілаў 2005 §18's alternation of у (data/names/w_names.tsv). §18 turns an unstressed initial У into Ў after a vowel and the reverse direction undoes it; Belarusian also writes Ў at the start of a borrowed name for English W, and Narkamaŭka keeps that Ў. After a vowel the two are indistinguishable, so reversing a name would corrupt it. This file is the list of stems where the Ў stays, and it is NORMATIVE: a port that does not read it will corrupt every W-name that follows a vowel. The file is TSV, so this schema describes the file dialect in `x-tsv` and the object each data line parses into in `$defs/row`.

declaration.description: The file declares the schema it is written against and its column order, as the stem inventory does, so the column order is a fact about the file rather than a fact about the parser.

columns.name: stem
columns.description: The stem, lowercase, always beginning with ў. Matching is by PREFIX on the lowercased word, so one stem covers a whole paradigm: ўотэрз matches Ўотэрзам, ўіл matches Ўіла. Take the first word of the name; the remaining words of a multi-word name are matched as tokens of their own.

columns.name: provenance
columns.description: Where the row came from. `hand` rows were read off an attested sentence in data/eval/tarask/gold_t2n.tsv — a stronger warrant than a label pair, so they are never overwritten by mining. `wikidata` rows come from an item whose English label begins with W and whose be-tarask label begins with Ў.

columns.name: evidence
columns.description: What backs the row: the gold file path for `hand`, or `<QID> <English label>` for `wikidata`.

x-openEnded: This inventory is open-ended by nature and cannot be completed. A W-name nobody has written down will still come back from T → N with У. That is a stated limit of rule morph.initial_u_w, recorded in data/NORMS.md; it is not a defect this file can close.
